|401|Unauthorized|If the issue tracker is private and the request was not authenticated.|None|
|404|Not Found|The specified repository or issue does not exist or does not have the issue tracker enabled.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: issue:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List changes on an issue

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/issues/string/changes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/changes`

Returns the list of all changes that have been made to the specified
issue. Changes are returned in chronological order with the oldest
change first.

Each time an issue is edited in the UI or through the API, an immutable
change record is created under the `/issues/123/changes` endpoint. It
also has a comment associated with the change.

Note that this operation is changing significantly, due to privacy changes.
See the [announcement](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/bitbucket-api-changes-gdpr/#changes-to-the-issue-changes-api)
for details.

```
$ curl -s https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/evzijst/dogslow/issues/1/changes - | jq .

{
  "pagelen": 20,
  "values": [
    {
      "changes": {
        "priority": {
          "new": "trivial",
          "old": "major"
        },
        "assignee": {
          "new": "",
          "old": "evzijst"
        },
        "assignee_account_id": {
          "new": "",
          "old": "557058:c0b72ad0-1cb5-4018-9cdc-0cde8492c443"
        },
        "kind": {
          "new": "enhancement",
          "old": "bug"
        }
      },
      "links": {
        "self": {
          "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/evzijst/dogslow/issues/1/changes/2"
        },
        "html": {
          "href": "https://bitbucket.org/evzijst/dogslow/issues/1#comment-2"
        }
      },
      "issue": {
        "links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/evzijst/dogslow/issues/1"
          }
        },
        "type": "issue",
        "id": 1,
        "repository": {
          "links": {
            "self": {
              "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/evzijst/dogslow"
            },
            "html": {
              "href": "https://bitbucket.org/evzijst/dogslow"
            },
            "avatar": {
              "href": "https://bitbucket.org/evzijst/dogslow/avatar/32/"
            }
          },
          "type": "repository",
          "name": "dogslow",
          "full_name": "evzijst/dogslow",
          "uuid": "{988b17c6-1a47-4e70-84ee-854d5f012bf6}"
        },
        "title": "Updated title"
      },
      "created_on": "2018-03-03T00:35:28.353630+00:00",
      "user": {
        "username": "evzijst",
        "nickname": "evzijst",
        "display_name": "evzijst",
        "type": "user",
        "uuid": "{aaa7972b-38af-4fb1-802d-6e3854c95778}",
        "links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/users/evzijst"
          },
          "html": {
            "href": "https://bitbucket.org/evzijst/"
          },
          "avatar": {
            "href": "https://bitbucket.org/account/evzijst/avatar/32/"
          }
        }
      },
      "message": {
        "raw": "Removed assignee, changed kind and priority.",
        "markup": "markdown",
        "html": "<p>Removed assignee, changed kind and priority.</p>",
        "type": "rendered"
      },
      "type": "issue_change",
      "id": 2
    }
  ],
  "page": 1
}
```

Changes support [filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) that
can be used to search for specific changes. For instance, to see
when an issue transitioned to "resolved":

```
$ curl -s https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/site/master/issues/1/changes \
   -G --data-urlencode='q=changes.state.new = "resolved"'
```

This resource is only available on repositories that have the issue
tracker enabled.

N.B.

The `changes.assignee` and `changes.assignee_account_id` fields are not
a `user` object. Instead, they contain the raw `username` and
`account_id` of the user. This is to protect the integrity of the audit
log even after a user account gets deleted.

The `changes.assignee` field is deprecated will disappear in the
future. Use `changes.assignee_account_id` instead.

<h3 id="list-changes-on-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|q|query|string|false|<br>Query string to narrow down the response. See<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for details.|
|sort|query|string|false|<br>Name of a response property to sort results. See<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#sorting-query-results)<br>for details.<br>|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The issue id|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="list-changes-on-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns all the issue changes that were made on the specified issue.|[paginated_log_entries](#schemapaginated_log_entries)|
|404|Not Found|The specified repository or issue does not exist or does not have the issue tracker enabled.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: issue ), basic, api_key
</aside>

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/changes`

Makes a change to the specified issue.

For example, to change an issue's state and assignee, create a new
change object that modifies these fields:

```
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/site/master/issues/1234/changes \
  -s -u evzijst -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "changes": {
      "assignee_account_id": {
        "new": "557058:c0b72ad0-1cb5-4018-9cdc-0cde8492c443"
      },
      "state": {
        "new": 'resolved"
      }
    }
    "message": {
      "raw": "This is now resolved."
    }
  }'
```

The above example also includes a custom comment to go alongside the
change. This comment will also be visible on the issue page in the UI.

The fields of the `changes` object are strings, not objects. This
allows for immutable change log records, even after user accounts,
milestones, or other objects recorded in a change entry, get renamed or
deleted.

The `assignee_account_id` field stores the account id. When POSTing a
new change and changing the assignee, the client should therefore use
the user's account_id in the `changes.assignee_account_id.new` field.

This call requires authentication. Private repositories or private
issue trackers require the caller to authenticate with an account that
has appropriate authorization.

<h3 id="modify-the-state-of-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The newly created issue change.|[issue_change](#schemaissue_change)|
|401|Unauthorized|When the request wasn't authenticated.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|When the authenticated user isn't authorized to modify the issue.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The specified repository or issue does not exist or does not have the issue tracker enabled.|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||The (absolute) URL of the newly created issue change.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: issue:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get issue change object

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/issues/string/changes/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/changes/{change_id}`

Returns the specified issue change object.

This resource is only available on repositories that have the issue
tracker enabled.

<h3 id="get-issue-change-object-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|change_id|path|string|true|The issue change id|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The issue id|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## List comments on an issue

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/issues/string/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/comments`

Returns a paginated list of all comments that were made on the
specified issue.

The default sorting is oldest to newest and can be overridden with
the `sort` query parameter.

This endpoint also supports filtering and sorting of the results. See
[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for more details.

<h3 id="list-comments-on-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|q|query|string|false|<br>Query string to narrow down the response as per<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering).|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The issue id|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Create a comment on an issue

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/issues/string/comments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "content": {
      "html": "string",
      "markup": "markdown",
      "raw": "string"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/comments`

Creates a new issue comment.

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/prlinks/issues/42/comments/ \
  -X POST -u evzijst \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"content": {"raw": "Lorem ipsum."}}'
```

<h3 id="create-a-comment-on-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The issue id|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[issue_comment](#schemaissue_comment)|true|The new issue comment object.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» content|body|object|false|none|
|» » html|body|string|false|The user's content rendered as HTML.|
|» » markup|body|string|false|The type of markup language the raw content is to be interpreted in.|
|» » raw|body|string|false|The text as it was typed by a user.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» deleted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|none|
|» inline|body|object|false|none|
|» » from|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the old version of the file.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The path of the file this comment is anchored to.|
|» » to|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the new version of the file. If the 'from' line is also provided, this value will be removed.|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » code|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » html|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» parent|body|[comment](#schemacomment)|false|none|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» user|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» issue|body|[issue](#schemaissue)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » markup|markdown|
|» » markup|creole|
|» » markup|plaintext|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-comment-on-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The newly created comment.|None|
|400|Bad Request|If the input was invalid, or if the comment being created is detected as spam |[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||The location of the newly issue comment.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: issue:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a comment on an issue

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/issues/string/comments/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/comments/{comment_id}`

Returns the specified issue comment object.

<h3 id="get-a-comment-on-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer|true|The id of the comment.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The issue id|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: issue ), basic, api_key
</aside>

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/comments/{comment_id}`

Updates the content of the specified issue comment. Note that only
the `content.raw` field can be modified.

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/prlinks/issues/42/comments/5728901 \
  -X PUT -u evzijst \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"content": {"raw": "Lorem ipsum."}'
```

<h3 id="update-a-comment-on-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer|true|The id of the comment.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The issue id|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[issue_comment](#schemaissue_comment)|true|The updated comment.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» content|body|object|false|none|
|» » html|body|string|false|The user's content rendered as HTML.|
|» » markup|body|string|false|The type of markup language the raw content is to be interpreted in.|
|» » raw|body|string|false|The text as it was typed by a user.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» deleted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|none|
|» inline|body|object|false|none|
|» » from|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the old version of the file.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The path of the file this comment is anchored to.|
|» » to|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the new version of the file. If the 'from' line is also provided, this value will be removed.|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » code|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » html|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» parent|body|[comment](#schemacomment)|false|none|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» user|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» issue|body|[issue](#schemaissue)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » markup|markdown|
|» » markup|creole|
|» » markup|plaintext|

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/deployments_config/environments/{environment_uuid}/variables`

Create a deployment environment level variable.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "secured": true,
  "uuid": "string",
  "value": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-variable-for-an-environment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|environment_uuid|path|string|true|The environment.|
|body|body|[deployment_variable](#schemadeployment_variable)|true|The variable to create|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» key|body|string|false|The unique name of the variable.|
|» secured|body|boolean|false|If true, this variable will be treated as secured. The value will never be exposed in the logs or the REST API.|
|» uuid|body|string|false|The UUID identifying the variable.|
|» value|body|string|false|The value of the variable. If the variable is secured, this will be empty.|

```json
  "key": "string",
  "secured": true,
  "uuid": "string",
  "value": "string"
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/`

Endpoint to create and initiate a pipeline.
There are a couple of different options to initiate a pipeline, where the payload of the request will determine which type of pipeline will be instantiated.
# Trigger a Pipeline for a branch
One way to trigger pipelines is by specifying the branch for which you want to trigger a pipeline.
The specified branch will be used to determine which pipeline definition from the `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file will be applied to initiate the pipeline. The pipeline will then do a clone of the repository and checkout the latest revision of the specified branch.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u username:password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/jeroendr/meat-demo2/pipelines/ \
  -d '
  {
    "target": {
      "ref_type": "branch",
      "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
      "ref_name": "master"
    }
  }'
```
# Trigger a Pipeline for a commit on a branch or tag
You can initiate a pipeline for a specific commit and in the context of a specified reference (e.g. a branch, tag or bookmark).
The specified reference will be used to determine which pipeline definition from the bitbucket-pipelines.yml file will be applied to initiate the pipeline. The pipeline will clone the repository and then do a checkout the specified reference.

The following reference types are supported:

* `branch`
* `named_branch`
* `bookmark`
 * `tag`

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u username:password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/jeroendr/meat-demo2/pipelines/ \
  -d '
  {
    "target": {
      "commit": {
        "type": "commit",
        "hash": "ce5b7431602f7cbba007062eeb55225c6e18e956"
      },
      "ref_type": "branch",
      "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
      "ref_name": "master"
    }
  }'
```
# Trigger a specific pipeline definition for a commit
You can trigger a specific pipeline that is defined in your `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file for a specific commit.
In addition to the commit revision, you specify the type and pattern of the selector that identifies the pipeline definition. The resulting pipeline will then clone the repository and checkout the specified revision.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u username:password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/jeroendr/meat-demo2/pipelines/ \
 -d '
  {
     "target": {
      "commit": {
         "hash":"a3c4e02c9a3755eccdc3764e6ea13facdf30f923",
         "type":"commit"
       },
        "selector": {
           "type":"custom",
              "pattern":"Deploy to production"
          },
        "type":"pipeline_commit_target"
   }
  }'
```
# Trigger a specific pipeline definition for a commit on a branch or tag
You can trigger a specific pipeline that is defined in your `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file for a specific commit in the context of a specified reference.
In addition to the commit revision, you specify the type and pattern of the selector that identifies the pipeline definition, as well as the reference information. The resulting pipeline will then clone the repository a checkout the specified reference.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u username:password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/jeroendr/meat-demo2/pipelines/ \
 -d '
  {
     "target": {
      "commit": {
         "hash":"a3c4e02c9a3755eccdc3764e6ea13facdf30f923",
         "type":"commit"
       },
       "selector": {
          "type": "custom",
          "pattern": "Deploy to production"
       },
       "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
       "ref_name": "master",
       "ref_type": "branch"
     }
  }'
```


# Trigger a custom pipeline with variables
In addition to triggering a custom pipeline that is defined in your `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` file as shown in the examples above, you can specify variables that will be available for your build. In the request, provide a list of variables, specifying the following for each variable: key, value, and whether it should be secured or not (this field is optional and defaults to not secured).

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u username:password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
 -d '
  {
    "target": {
      "type": "pipeline_ref_target",
      "ref_type": "branch",
      "ref_name": "master",
      "selector": {
        "type": "custom",
        "pattern": "Deploy to production"
      }
    },
    "variables": [
      {
        "key": "var1key",
        "value": "var1value",
        "secured": true
      },
      {
        "key": "var2key",
        "value": "var2value"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

# Trigger a pull request pipeline

You can also initiate a pipeline for a specific pull request.

### Example

```
$ curl -X POST -is -u username:password \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/ \
 -d '
  {
	"target": {
      "type": "pipeline_pullrequest_target",
	  "source": "pull-request-branch",
      "destination": "master",
      "destination_commit": {
      	 "hash" : "9f848b7"
      },
      "commit": {
      	"hash" : "1a372fc"
      },
      "pullrequest" : {
      	"id" : "3"
      },
	  "selector": {
        "type": "pull-requests",
        "pattern": "**"
      }
    }
  }'
```

## Get log file for a step

<a id="opIdgetPipelineStepLogForRepository"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pipelines/string/steps/string/log
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/{pipeline_uuid}/steps/{step_uuid}/log`

Retrieve the log file for a given step of a pipeline.

This endpoint supports (and encourages!) the use of [HTTP Range requests](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7233) to deal with potentially very large log files.

<h3 id="get-log-file-for-a-step-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|pipeline_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the pipeline.|
|step_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the step.|

<h3 id="get-log-file-for-a-step-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The raw log file for this pipeline step.|None|
|304|Not Modified|The log has the same etag as the provided If-None-Match header.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|A pipeline with the given UUID does not exist, a step with the given UUID does not exist in the pipeline or a log file does not exist for the given step.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|416|Range Not Satisfiable|The requested range does not exist for requests that specified the [HTTP Range header](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7233#section-3.1).|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines/{pipeline_uuid}/steps/{step_uuid}/logs/{log_uuid}`

Retrieve the log file for a build container or service container.

This endpoint supports (and encourages!) the use of [HTTP Range requests](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7233) to deal with potentially very large log files.

<h3 id="get-the-logs-for-the-build-container-or-a-service-container-for-a-given-step-of-a-pipeline-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository.|
|pipeline_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the pipeline.|
|step_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of the step.|
|log_uuid|path|string|true|For the main build container specify the step UUID; for a service container specify the service container UUID|

<h3 id="get-the-logs-for-the-build-container-or-a-service-container-for-a-given-step-of-a-pipeline-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The raw log file for the build container or service container.|None|
|404|Not Found|No account, repository, pipeline, step or log exist for the provided path.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
```

## Update the next build number

<a id="opIdupdateRepositoryBuildNumber"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pipelines_config/build_number \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "next": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pipelines_config/build_number`

Update the next build number that should be assigned to a pipeline. The next build number that will be configured has to be strictly higher than the current latest build number for this repository.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "next": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-next-build-number-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces, for example `{workspace UUID}`.|

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-projects">Projects</h1>

Bitbucket Cloud projects make it easier for teams to focus on
a goal, product, or process by organizing their repositories.


## Create a project in a workspace

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/workspaces/string/projects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "description": "string",
    "has_publicly_visible_repos": true,
    "is_private": true,
    "key": "string",
    "links": {
      "avatar": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "html": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      }
    },
    "name": "string",
    "owner": {
      "type": "string",
      "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "display_name": "string",
      "links": {
        "avatar": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        },
        "html": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        },
        "members": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        },
        "projects": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        },
        "repositories": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        },
        "self": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        }
      },
      "username": "string",
      "uuid": "string"
    },
    "updated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "uuid": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /workspaces/{workspace}/projects`

Creates a new project.

Note that the avatar has to be embedded as either a data-url
or a URL to an external image as shown in the examples below:

```
$ body=$(cat << EOF
{
    "name": "Mars Project",
    "key": "MARS",
    "description": "Software for colonizing mars.",
    "links": {
        "avatar": {
            "href": "data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhEAAQAMQAAORHHOVSKudfOulrSOp3WOyDZu6QdvCchPGolfO0o/..."
        }
    },
    "is_private": false
}
EOF
)
$ curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -X POST \
       -d "$body" \
       https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/teams/teams-in-space/projects/ | jq .
{
  // Serialized project document
}
```

or even:

```
$ body=$(cat << EOF
{
    "name": "Mars Project",
    "key": "MARS",
    "description": "Software for colonizing mars.",
    "links": {
        "avatar": {
            "href": "http://i.imgur.com/72tRx4w.gif"
        }
    },
    "is_private": false
}
EOF
)
$ curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -X POST \
       -d "$body" \
       https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/teams/teams-in-space/projects/ | jq .
{
  // Serialized project document
}
```

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "description": "string",
  "has_publicly_visible_repos": true,
  "is_private": true,
  "key": "string",
  "links": {
    "avatar": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    },
    "html": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    }
  },
  "name": "string",
  "owner": {
    "type": "string",
    "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "display_name": "string",
    "links": {
      "avatar": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "html": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "members": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      },
      "projects": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
```

`PUT /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}`

Since this endpoint can be used to both update and to create a
project, the request body depends on the intent.

#### Creation

See the POST documentation for the project collection for an
example of the request body.

Note: The `key` should not be specified in the body of request
(since it is already present in the URL). The `name` is required,
everything else is optional.

#### Update

See the POST documentation for the project collection for an
example of the request body.

Note: The key is not required in the body (since it is already in
the URL). The key may be specified in the body, if the intent is
to change the key itself. In such a scenario, the location of the
project is changed and is returned in the `Location` header of the
response.

## Delete a project for a workspace

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/workspaces/string/projects/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}`

Deletes this project. This is an irreversible operation.

You cannot delete a project that still contains repositories.
To delete the project, [delete](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-repositories/#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-delete)
or transfer the repositories first.

Example:
```
$ curl -X DELETE https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/bbworkspace1/PROJ
```

<h3 id="delete-a-project-for-a-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_key|path|string|true|The project in question. This is the actual `key` assigned<br>to the project.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-project-for-a-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Successful deletion.|None|
|403|Forbidden|The requesting user isn't authorized to delete the project or the project isn't empty.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|A project isn't hosted at this location.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">

## List the default reviewers in a project

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/workspaces/string/projects/string/default-reviewers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}/default-reviewers`

Return a list of all default reviewers for a project. This is a list of users that will be added as default
reviewers to pull requests for any repository within the project.

Example:
```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/.../projects/.../default-reviewers | jq .
{
    "pagelen": 10,
    "values": [
        {
            "user": {
                "display_name": "Davis Lee",
                "uuid": "{f0e0e8e9-66c1-4b85-a784-44a9eb9ef1a6}"

                "uuid": "{1aa43376-260d-4a0b-9660-f62672b9655d}"
            },
            "reviewer_type": "project",
            "type": "default_reviewer"

    ],
    "page": 1,

}
```

## Get a default reviewer

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}/default-reviewers/{selected_user}`

Returns the specified default reviewer.

Example:
```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/.../default-reviewers/%7Bf0e0e8e9-66c1-4b85-a784-44a9eb9ef1a6%7D
{
    "display_name": "Davis Lee",
```

|project_key|path|string|true|The project in question. This can either be the actual `key` assigned<br>to the project or the `UUID` (surrounded by curly-braces (`{}`)).<br>|
|selected_user|path|string|true|This can either be the username or the UUID of the default reviewer,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|


## Add the specific user as a default reviewer for the project

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/workspaces/string/projects/string/default-reviewers/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /workspaces/{workspace}/projects/{project_key}/default-reviewers/{selected_user}`

Adds the specified user to the project's list of default reviewers. The method is
idempotent. Accepts an optional body containing the `uuid` of the user to be added.

Example:
```
$ curl -XPUT https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/.../default-reviewers/%7Bf0e0e8e9-66c1-4b85-a784-44a9eb9ef1a6%7D
-d { 'uuid': '{f0e0e8e9-66c1-4b85-a784-44a9eb9ef1a6}' }

HTTP/1.1 204
```

<h3 id="add-the-specific-user-as-a-default-reviewer-for-the-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_key|path|string|true|The project in question. This can either be the actual `key` assigned<br>to the project or the `UUID` (surrounded by curly-braces (`{}`)).<br>|
|selected_user|path|string|true|This can either be the username or the UUID of the default reviewer,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-pullrequests">Pullrequests</h1>

Pull requests are a feature that makes it easier for developers
to collaborate using Bitbucket. They provide a user-friendly web
interface for discussing proposed changes before integrating them
into the official project.


## List pull requests for a user

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/pullrequests/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /pullrequests/{selected_user}`

Returns all pull requests authored by the specified user.

By default only open pull requests are returned. This can be controlled
using the `state` query parameter. To retrieve pull requests that are
in one of multiple states, repeat the `state` parameter for each
individual state.

This endpoint also supports filtering and sorting of the results. See
[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for more details.

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-for-a-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|state|query|string|false|Only return pull requests that are in this state. This parameter can be repeated.|
|selected_user|path|string|true|This can either be the username of the pull request author, the author's UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`, or the author's Atlassian ID.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|OPEN|
|state|MERGED|
|state|DECLINED|
|state|SUPERSEDED|

</aside>

## List pull requests that contain a commit

<a id="opIdgetPullrequestsForCommit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/commit/string/pullrequests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/commit/{commit}/pullrequests`

Returns a paginated list of all pull requests as part of which this commit was reviewed. Pull Request Commit Links app must be installed first before using this API; installation automatically occurs when 'Go to pull request' is clicked from the web interface for a commit's details.

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-that-contain-a-commit-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID surrounded by curly-braces|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|The repository; either the UUID in curly braces, or the slug|
|commit|path|string|true|The SHA1 of the commit|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|Which page to retrieve|
|pagelen|query|integer(int32)|false|How many pull requests to retrieve per page|

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-that-contain-a-commit-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The paginated list of pull requests.|[paginated_pullrequests](#schemapaginated_pullrequests)|
|202|Accepted|The repository's pull requests are still being indexed.|[paginated_pullrequests](#schemapaginated_pullrequests)|
|404|Not Found|Either the repository does not exist, or pull request commit links have not yet been indexed.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List default reviewers

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/default-reviewers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/default-reviewers`

Returns the repository's default reviewers.

These are the users that are automatically added as reviewers on every
new pull request that is created. To obtain the repository's default reviewers
as well as the default reviewers inherited from the project, use the
[effective-default-reveiwers](#api-repositories-workspace-repo-slug-effective-default-reviewers-get) endpoint.

<h3 id="list-default-reviewers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "next": "http://example.com",
  "page": 1,
  "pagelen": 1,
  "previous": "http://example.com",
  "size": 0,
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "string",
      "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "display_name": "string",
      "links": {
        "avatar": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        }
      },
      "username": "string",
      "uuid": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-default-reviewers-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The paginated list of default reviewers|[paginated_accounts](#schemapaginated_accounts)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to view the default reviewers|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a default reviewer

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/default-reviewers/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/default-reviewers/{target_username}`

Returns the specified reviewer.

This can be used to test whether a user is among the repository's
default reviewers list. A 404 indicates that that specified user is not
a default reviewer.

<h3 id="get-a-default-reviewer-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|target_username|path|string|true|This can either be the username or the UUID of the default reviewer,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
```

## Add a user to the default reviewers

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/default-reviewers/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/default-reviewers/{target_username}`

Adds the specified user to the repository's list of default
reviewers.

This method is idempotent. Adding a user a second time has no effect.

<h3 id="add-a-user-to-the-default-reviewers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|target_username|path|string|true|This can either be the username or the UUID of the default reviewer,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{account UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## List effective default reviewers

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/effective-default-reviewers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/effective-default-reviewers`

Returns the repository's effective default reviewers. This includes both default
reviewers defined at the repository level as well as those inherited from its project.

These are the users that are automatically added as reviewers on every
new pull request that is created.

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/{workspace_slug}/{repo_slug}/effective-default-reviewers?page=1&pagelen=20
```

## List pull requests

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests`

Returns all pull requests on the specified repository.

By default only open pull requests are returned. This can be controlled
using the `state` query parameter. To retrieve pull requests that are
in one of multiple states, repeat the `state` parameter for each
individual state.

This endpoint also supports filtering and sorting of the results. See
[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for more details.

<h3 id="list-pull-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|state|query|string|false|Only return pull requests that are in this state. This parameter can be repeated.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|OPEN|
|state|MERGED|
|state|DECLINED|
|state|SUPERSEDED|

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests`

Creates a new pull request where the destination repository is
this repository and the author is the authenticated user.

The minimum required fields to create a pull request are `title` and
`source`, specified by a branch name.

```
curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/my-workspace/my-repository/pullrequests \
    -u my-username:my-password \
    --request POST \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{
        "title": "My Title",
        "source": {
            "branch": {
                "name": "staging"
            }
        }
    }'
```

If the pull request's `destination` is not specified, it will default
to the `repository.mainbranch`. To open a pull request to a
different branch, say from a feature branch to a staging branch,
specify a `destination` (same format as the `source`):

```
{
    "title": "My Title",
    "source": {
        "branch": {
            "name": "my-feature-branch"
        }
    },
    "destination": {
        "branch": {
            "name": "staging"
        }
    }
}
```

Reviewers can be specified by adding an array of user objects as the
`reviewers` property.

```
{
    "title": "My Title",
    "source": {
        "branch": {
            "name": "my-feature-branch"
        }
    },
    "reviewers": [
        {
            "uuid": "{504c3b62-8120-4f0c-a7bc-87800b9d6f70}"
        }
    ]
}
```

Other fields:

* `description` - a string
* `close_source_branch` - boolean that specifies if the source branch should be closed upon merging

<h3 id="create-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|The new pull request.<br><br>The request URL you POST to becomes the destination repository URL. For this reason, you must specify an explicit source repository in the request object if you want to pull from a different repository (fork).<br><br>Since not all elements are required or even mutable, you only need to include the elements you want to initialize, such as the source branch and the title.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» author|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» close_source_branch|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag indicating if merging the pull request closes the source branch.|
|» closed_by|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» comment_count|body|integer|false|The number of comments for a specific pull request.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was created.|
|» destination|body|[pullrequest_endpoint](#schemapullrequest_endpoint)|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|The pull request's unique ID. Note that pull request IDs are only unique within their associated repository.|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » activity|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » approve|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » comments|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » commits|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » decline|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|

<h3 id="create-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The newly created pull request.|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|
|400|Bad Request|If the input document was invalid, or if the caller lacks the privilege to create repositories under the targeted account.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|If the request was not authenticated.|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||The URL of new newly created pull request.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List a pull request activity log

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/activity \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/activity`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's activity log.

This handler serves both a v20 and internal endpoint. The v20 endpoint
returns reviewer comments, updates, approvals and request changes. The internal
endpoint includes those plus tasks and attachments.

Comments created on a file or a line of code have an inline property.

Comment example:

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The pull request activity log|None|
|401|Unauthorized|If the repository is private and the request was not authenticated.|None|
|404|Not Found|If the specified repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}`

Returns the specified pull request.

<h3 id="get-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

`PUT /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}`

Mutates the specified pull request.

This can be used to change the pull request's branches or description.

Only open pull requests can be mutated.

<h3 id="update-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|The pull request that is to be updated.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» author|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» close_source_branch|body|boolean|false|A boolean flag indicating if merging the pull request closes the source branch.|
|» closed_by|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» comment_count|body|integer|false|The number of comments for a specific pull request.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was created.|
|» destination|body|[pullrequest_endpoint](#schemapullrequest_endpoint)|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|The pull request's unique ID. Note that pull request IDs are only unique within their associated repository.|

|» participants|body|[[participant](#schemaparticipant)]|false|        The list of users that are collaborating on this pull request.<br>        Collaborators are user that:<br><br>        * are added to the pull request as a reviewer (part of the reviewers<br>          list)<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have commented on the pull request<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have approved the pull request<br><br>        Each user is wrapped in an object that indicates the user's role and<br>        whether they have approved the pull request. For performance reasons,<br>        the API only returns this list when an API requests a pull request by<br>        id.<br>        |

## List a pull request activity log

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/activity \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/activity`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's activity log.

This handler serves both a v20 and internal endpoint. The v20 endpoint
returns reviewer comments, updates, approvals and request changes. The internal
endpoint includes those plus tasks and attachments.

Comments created on a file or a line of code have an inline property.

## Approve a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/approve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/approve`

Approve the specified pull request as the authenticated user.

<h3 id="approve-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "approved": true,
  "participated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "role": "PARTICIPANT",
  "state": "approved",
  "user": {
    "type": "string",
    "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "display_name": "string",
    "links": {
      "avatar": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      }
    },
    "username": "string",
    "uuid": "string"
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {

    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
```

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="approve-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The `participant` object recording that the authenticated user approved the pull request.|[participant](#schemaparticipant)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request wasn't authenticated.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The specified pull request or the repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Unapprove a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/approve \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/approve`

Redact the authenticated user's approval of the specified pull
request.

<h3 id="unapprove-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

```json
{

    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="unapprove-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|An empty response indicating the authenticated user's approval has been withdrawn.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Pull request cannot be unapproved because the pull request has already been merged.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request wasn't authenticated.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The specified pull request or the repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List comments on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/comments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's comments.

This includes both global, inline comments and replies.

The default sorting is oldest to newest and can be overridden with
the `sort` query parameter.

This endpoint also supports filtering and sorting of the results. See
[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for more
details.

<h3 id="list-comments-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="list-comments-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A paginated list of comments made on the given pull request, in chronological order.|[paginated_pullrequest_comments](#schemapaginated_pullrequest_comments)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to the pull request.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the pull request does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h3 id="create-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest_comment](#schemapullrequest_comment)|true|The comment object.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» content|body|object|false|none|
|» » html|body|string|false|The user's content rendered as HTML.|
|» » markup|body|string|false|The type of markup language the raw content is to be interpreted in.|
|» » raw|body|string|false|The text as it was typed by a user.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» deleted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|none|
|» inline|body|object|false|none|
|» » from|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the old version of the file.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The path of the file this comment is anchored to.|
|» » to|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the new version of the file. If the 'from' line is also provided, this value will be removed.|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » code|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » html|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» parent|body|[comment](#schemacomment)|false|none|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» user|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» pullrequest|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » markup|markdown|
|» » markup|creole|
|» » markup|plaintext|

<h3 id="create-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The newly created comment.|[pullrequest_comment](#schemapullrequest_comment)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to the pull request.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the pull request does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|Location|string||The URL of the new comment|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get a comment on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/comments/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments/{comment_id}`

Returns a specific pull request comment.

<h3 id="get-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer|true|The id of the comment.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="update-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer|true|The id of the comment.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest_comment](#schemapullrequest_comment)|true|The contents of the updated comment.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|
|» content|body|object|false|none|
|» » html|body|string|false|The user's content rendered as HTML.|
|» » markup|body|string|false|The type of markup language the raw content is to be interpreted in.|
|» » raw|body|string|false|The text as it was typed by a user.|
|» created_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» deleted|body|boolean|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|false|none|
|» inline|body|object|false|none|
|» » from|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the old version of the file.|
|» » path|body|string|true|The path of the file this comment is anchored to.|
|» » to|body|integer|false|The comment's anchor line in the new version of the file. If the 'from' line is also provided, this value will be removed.|
|» links|body|object|false|none|
|» » code|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » html|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » self|body|object|false|A link to a resource related to this object.|
|» » » href|body|string(uri)|false|none|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» parent|body|[comment](#schemacomment)|false|none|
|» updated_on|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» user|body|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» pullrequest|body|[pullrequest](#schemapullrequest)|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » markup|markdown|
|» » markup|creole|
|» » markup|plaintext|

<h3 id="update-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The updated comment.|[pullrequest_comment](#schemapullrequest_comment)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to the comment.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the comment does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Delete a comment on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/comments/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/comments/{comment_id}`

Deletes a specific pull request comment.

<h3 id="delete-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|comment_id|path|integer|true|The id of the comment.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-comment-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Successful deletion.|None|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to delete the comment.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the comment does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## List commits on a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/commits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/commits`

Returns a paginated list of the pull request's commits.

These are the commits that are being merged into the destination
branch when the pull requests gets accepted.

<h3 id="list-commits-on-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-commits-on-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A paginated list of commits made on the given pull request, in chronological order. This list will be empty if the source branch no longer exists.|None|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have access to the pull request.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the pull request does not exist or the source branch is from a forked repository which no longer exists.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Decline a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/decline \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/decline`

Declines the pull request.

<h3 id="decline-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

## Merge a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/merge \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "close_source_branch": true,
    "merge_strategy": "merge_commit",
    "message": "string",
    "type": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/merge`

Merges the pull request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "close_source_branch": true,
  "merge_strategy": "merge_commit",
  "message": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="merge-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|async|query|boolean|false|Default value is false.<br><br><br>When set to true, runs merge asynchronously and<br>immediately returns a 202 with polling link to<br>the task-status API in the Location header.<br><br><br>When set to false, runs merge and waits for it to<br>complete, returning 200 when it succeeds. If the<br>duration of the merge exceeds a timeout threshold,<br>the API returns a 202 with polling link to the<br>task-status API in the Location header.|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|
|body|body|[pullrequest_merge_parameters](#schemapullrequest_merge_parameters)|false|none|
|» close_source_branch|body|boolean|false|Whether the source branch should be deleted. If this is not provided, we fallback to the value used when the pull request was created, which defaults to False|
|» merge_strategy|body|string|false|The merge strategy that will be used to merge the pull request.|
|» message|body|string|false|The commit message that will be used on the resulting commit.|
|» type|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» merge_strategy|merge_commit|
|» merge_strategy|squash|
|» merge_strategy|fast_forward|

## Get the merge task status for a pull request

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/pullrequests/0/merge/task-status/string \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/pullrequests/{pull_request_id}/merge/task-status/{task_id}`

When merging a pull request takes too long, the client receives a
task ID along with a 202 status code. The task ID can be used in a call
to this endpoint to check the status of a merge task.

```
curl -X GET https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bitbucket/pullrequests/2286/merge/task-status/<task_id>
```

If the merge task is not yet finished, a PENDING status will be returned.

```
HTTP/2 200
{
    "task_status": "PENDING",
    "links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bitbucket/pullrequests/2286/merge/task-status/<task_id>"
        }
    }
}
```

If the merge was successful, a SUCCESS status will be returned.

```
HTTP/2 200
{
    "task_status": "SUCCESS",
    "links": {
        "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bitbucket/pullrequests/2286/merge/task-status/<task_id>"
        }
    },
    "merge_result": <the merged pull request object>
}
```

If the merge task failed, an error will be returned.

```
{
    "type": "error",
    "error": {
        "message": "<error message>"
    }
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-merge-task-status-for-a-pull-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pull_request_id|path|integer|true|The id of the pull request.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|task_id|path|string|true|ID of the merge task|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

<h3 id="get-the-merge-task-status-for-a-pull-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a task status if the merge is either pending or successful, and if it is successful, a pull request|None|
|400|Bad Request|If the provided task ID does not relate to this pull request, or if something went wrong during the merge operation|None|
|403|Forbidden|The user making the request does not have permission to the repo and is different from the user who queued the task|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: pullrequest ), basic, api_key
</aside>
