<h1 id="bitbucket-api-source">Source</h1>

Browse the source code in the repository and
                              create new commits by uploading.

## List commits that modified a file

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/filehistory/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/filehistory/{commit}/{path}`

Returns a paginated list of commits that modified the specified file.

Commits are returned in reverse chronological order. This is roughly
equivalent to the following commands:

    $ git log --follow --date-order <sha> <path>

By default, Bitbucket will follow renames and the path name in the
returned entries reflects that. This can be turned off using the
`?renames=false` query parameter.

Results are returned in descending chronological order by default, and
like most endpoints you can
[filter and sort](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) the response to
only provide exactly the data you want.

For example, if you wanted to find commits made before 2011-05-18
against a file named `README.rst`, but you only wanted the path and
date, your query would look like this:

```
$ curl 'https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/evzijst/dogslow/filehistory/master/README.rst'\
  '?fields=values.next,values.path,values.commit.date&q=commit.date<=2011-05-18'
{
  "values": [
    {
      "commit": {
        "date": "2011-05-17T07:32:09+00:00"
      },
      "path": "README.rst"
    },
    {
      "commit": {
        "date": "2011-05-16T06:33:28+00:00"
      },
      "path": "README.txt"
    },
    {
      "commit": {
        "date": "2011-05-16T06:15:39+00:00"
      },
      "path": "README.txt"
    }
  ]
}
```

In the response you can see that the file was renamed to `README.rst`
by the commit made on 2011-05-16, and was previously named `README.txt`.

<h3 id="list-commits-that-modified-a-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|renames|query|string|false|<br>When `true`, Bitbucket will follow the history of the file across<br>renames (this is the default behavior). This can be turned off by<br>specifying `false`.|
|q|query|string|false|<br>Query string to narrow down the response as per<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering).|
|sort|query|string|false|<br>Name of a response property sort the result by as per<br>[filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#sorting-query-results).<br>|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|path|path|string|true|Path to the file.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "next": "http://example.com",
  "page": 1,
  "pagelen": 1,
  "previous": "http://example.com",
  "size": 0,
  "values": [
    {
      "attributes": "link",
      "commit": {
        "participants": [
          {
            "type": "string",
            "approved": true,
            "participated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "role": "PARTICIPANT",
            "state": "approved",
            "user": {
              "type": "string",
              "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
              "display_name": "string",
              "links": {
                "avatar": {
                  "href": "http://example.com",
                  "name": "string"
                }
              },
              "username": "string",
              "uuid": "string"
            }
          }
        ],
        "repository": {}
      },
      "escaped_path": "string",
      "path": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
```

## Create a commit by uploading a file

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/src \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/src`

This endpoint is used to create new commits in the repository by
uploading files.

To add a new file to a repository:

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/username/slug/src \
  -F /repo/path/to/image.png=@image.png
```

This will create a new commit on top of the main branch, inheriting the
contents of the main branch, but adding (or overwriting) the
`image.png` file to the repository in the `/repo/path/to` directory.

To create a commit that deletes files, use the `files` parameter:

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/username/slug/src \
  -F files=/file/to/delete/1.txt \
  -F files=/file/to/delete/2.txt
```

You can add/modify/delete multiple files in a request. Rename/move a
file by deleting the old path and adding the content at the new path.

This endpoint accepts `multipart/form-data` (as in the examples above),
as well as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

#### multipart/form-data

A `multipart/form-data` post contains a series of "form fields" that
identify both the individual files that are being uploaded, as well as
additional, optional meta data.

Files are uploaded in file form fields (those that have a
`Content-Disposition` parameter) whose field names point to the remote
path in the repository where the file should be stored. Path field
names are always interpreted to be absolute from the root of the
repository, regardless whether the client uses a leading slash (as the
above `curl` example did).

File contents are treated as bytes and are not decoded as text.

The commit message, as well as other non-file meta data for the
request, is sent along as normal form field elements. Meta data fields
share the same namespace as the file objects. For `multipart/form-data`
bodies that should not lead to any ambiguity, as the
`Content-Disposition` header will contain the `filename` parameter to
distinguish between a file named "message" and the commit message field.

#### application/x-www-form-urlencoded

It is also possible to upload new files using a simple
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` POST. This can be convenient when
uploading pure text files:

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src \
  --data-urlencode "/path/to/me.txt=Lorem ipsum." \
  --data-urlencode "message=Initial commit" \
  --data-urlencode "author=Erik van Zijst <erik.van.zijst@gmail.com>"
```

There could be a field name clash if a client were to upload a file
named "message", as this filename clashes with the meta data property
for the commit message. To avoid this and to upload files whose names
clash with the meta data properties, use a leading slash for the files,
e.g. `curl --data-urlencode "/message=file contents"`.

When an explicit slash is omitted for a file whose path matches that of
a meta data parameter, then it is interpreted as meta data, not as a
file.

#### Executables and links

While this API aims to facilitate the most common use cases, it is
possible to perform some more advanced operations like creating a new
symlink in the repository, or creating an executable file.

Files can be supplied with a `x-attributes` value in the
`Content-Disposition` header. For example, to upload an executable
file, as well as create a symlink from `README.txt` to `README`:

```
--===============1438169132528273974==
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="us-ascii"
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
Content-ID: "bin/shutdown.sh"
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="shutdown.sh"; x-attributes:"executable"

#!/bin/sh
halt

--===============1438169132528273974==
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="us-ascii"
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
Content-ID: "/README.txt"
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="README.txt"; x-attributes:"link"

README
--===============1438169132528273974==--
```

Links are files that contain the target path and have
`x-attributes:"link"` set.

When overwriting links with files, or vice versa, the newly uploaded
file determines both the new contents, as well as the attributes. That
means uploading a file without specifying `x-attributes="link"` will
create a regular file, even if the parent commit hosted a symlink at
the same path.

The same applies to executables. When modifying an existing executable
file, the form-data file element must include
`x-attributes="executable"` in order to preserve the executable status
of the file.

Note that this API does not support the creation or manipulation of
subrepos / submodules.

<h3 id="create-a-commit-by-uploading-a-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|query|string|false|The commit message. When omitted, Bitbucket uses a canned string.|
|author|query|string|false|<br>The raw string to be used as the new commit's author.<br>This string follows the format<br>`Erik van Zijst <evzijst@atlassian.com>`.<br><br>When omitted, Bitbucket uses the authenticated user's<br>full/display name and primary email address. Commits cannot<br>be created anonymously.|
|parents|query|string|false|<br>A comma-separated list of SHA1s of the commits that should<br>be the parents of the newly created commit.<br><br>When omitted, the new commit will inherit from and become<br>a child of the main branch's tip/HEAD commit.<br><br>When more than one SHA1 is provided, the first SHA1<br>identifies the commit from which the content will be<br>inherited.".|
|files|query|string|false|<br>Optional field that declares the files that the request is<br>manipulating. When adding a new file to a repo, or when<br>overwriting an existing file, the client can just upload<br>the full contents of the file in a normal form field and<br>the use of this `files` meta data field is redundant.<br>However, when the `files` field contains a file path that<br>does not have a corresponding, identically-named form<br>field, then Bitbucket interprets that as the client wanting<br>to replace the named file with the null set and the file is<br>deleted instead.<br><br>Paths in the repo that are referenced in neither files nor<br>an individual file field, remain unchanged and carry over<br>from the parent to the new commit.<br><br>This API does not support renaming as an explicit feature.<br>To rename a file, simply delete it and recreate it under<br>the new name in the same commit.<br>|
|branch|query|string|false|<br>The name of the branch that the new commit should be<br>created on. When omitted, the commit will be created on top<br>of the main branch and will become the main branch's new<br>head.<br><br>When a branch name is provided that already exists in the<br>repo, then the commit will be created on top of that<br>branch. In this case, *if* a parent SHA1 was also provided,<br>then it is asserted that the parent is the branch's<br>tip/HEAD at the time the request is made. When this is not<br>the case, a 409 is returned.<br><br>When a new branch name is specified (that does not already<br>exist in the repo), and no parent SHA1s are provided, then<br>the new commit will inherit from the current main branch's<br>tip/HEAD commit, but not advance the main branch. The new<br>commit will be the new branch. When the request *also*<br>specifies a parent SHA1, then the new commit and branch<br>are created directly on top of the parent commit,<br>regardless of the state of the main branch.<br><br>When a branch name is not specified, but a parent SHA1 is<br>provided, then Bitbucket asserts that it represents the<br>main branch's current HEAD/tip, or a 409 is returned.<br><br>When a branch name is not specified and the repo is empty,<br>the new commit will become the repo's root commit and will<br>be on the main branch.<br><br>When a branch name is specified and the repo is empty, the<br>new commit will become the repo's root commit and also<br>define the repo's main branch going forward.<br><br>This API cannot be used to create additional root commits<br>in non-empty repos.<br><br>The branch field cannot be repeated.<br><br>As a side effect, this API can be used to create a new<br>branch without modifying any files, by specifying a new<br>branch name in this field, together with `parents`, but<br>omitting the `files` fields, while not sending any files.<br>This will create a new commit and branch with the same<br>contents as the first parent. The diff of this commit<br>against its first parent will be empty.<br>|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-commit-by-uploading-a-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|<br>|None|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have write or admin access|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the repository does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository:write ), basic, api_key
</aside>

## Get file or directory contents

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/repositories/string/string/src/string/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /repositories/{workspace}/{repo_slug}/src/{commit}/{path}`

This endpoints is used to retrieve the contents of a single file,
or the contents of a directory at a specified revision.

#### Raw file contents

When `path` points to a file, this endpoint returns the raw contents.
The response's Content-Type is derived from the filename
extension (not from the contents). The file contents are not processed
and no character encoding/recoding is performed and as a result no
character encoding is included as part of the Content-Type.

The `Content-Disposition` header will be "attachment" to prevent
browsers from running executable files.

If the file is managed by LFS, then a 301 redirect pointing to
Atlassian's media services platform is returned.

The response includes an ETag that is based on the contents of the file
and its attributes. This means that an empty `__init__.py` always
returns the same ETag, regardless on the directory it lives in, or the
commit it is on.

#### File meta data

When the request for a file path includes the query parameter
`?format=meta`, instead of returning the file's raw contents, Bitbucket
instead returns the JSON object describing the file's properties:

```javascript
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef/tests/__init__.py?format=meta
{
  "links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/__init__.py"
    },
    "meta": {
      "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/__init__.py?format=meta"
    }
  },
  "path": "tests/__init__.py",
  "commit": {
    "type": "commit",
    "hash": "eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335",
    "links": {
      "self": {
        "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/commit/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335"
      },
      "html": {
        "href": "https://bitbucket.org/atlassian/bbql/commits/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335"
      }
    }
  },
  "attributes": [],
  "type": "commit_file",
  "size": 0
}
```

File objects contain an `attributes` element that contains a list of
possible modifiers. Currently defined values are:

* `link` -- indicates that the entry is a symbolic link. The contents
    of the file represent the path the link points to.
* `executable` -- indicates that the file has the executable bit set.
* `subrepository` -- indicates that the entry points to a submodule or
    subrepo. The contents of the file is the SHA1 of the repository
    pointed to.
* `binary` -- indicates whether Bitbucket thinks the file is binary.

This endpoint can provide an alternative to how a HEAD request can be
used to check for the existence of a file, or a file's size without
incurring the overhead of receiving its full contents.


#### Directory listings

When `path` points to a directory instead of a file, the response is a
paginated list of directory and file objects in the same order as the
underlying SCM system would return them.

For example:

```javascript
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef/tests
{
  "pagelen": 10,
  "values": [
    {
      "path": "tests/test_project",
      "type": "commit_directory",
      "links": {
        "self": {
          "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/test_project/"
        },
        "meta": {
          "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/test_project/?format=meta"
        }
      },
      "commit": {
        "type": "commit",
        "hash": "eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335",
        "links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/commit/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335"
          },
          "html": {
            "href": "https://bitbucket.org/atlassian/bbql/commits/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "links": {
        "self": {
          "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/__init__.py"
        },
        "meta": {
          "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/__init__.py?format=meta"
        }
      },
      "path": "tests/__init__.py",
      "commit": {
        "type": "commit",
        "hash": "eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335",
        "links": {
          "self": {
            "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/commit/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335"
          },
          "html": {
            "href": "https://bitbucket.org/atlassian/bbql/commits/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335"
          }
        }
      },
      "attributes": [],
      "type": "commit_file",
      "size": 0
    }
  ],
  "page": 1,
  "size": 2
}
```

When listing the contents of the repo's root directory, the use of a
trailing slash at the end of the URL is required.

The response by default is not recursive, meaning that only the direct contents of
a path are returned. The response does not recurse down into
subdirectories. In order to "walk" the entire directory tree, the
client can either parse each response and follow the `self` links of each
`commit_directory` object, or can specify a `max_depth` to recurse to.

The max_depth parameter will do a breadth-first search to return the contents of the subdirectories
up to the depth specified. Breadth-first search was chosen as it leads to the least amount of
file system operations for git. If the `max_depth` parameter is specified to be too
large, the call will time out and return a 555.

Each returned object is either a `commit_file`, or a `commit_directory`,
both of which contain a `path` element. This path is the absolute path
from the root of the repository. Each object also contains a `commit`
object which embeds the commit the file is on. Note that this is merely
the commit that was used in the URL. It is *not* the commit that last
modified the file.

Directory objects have 2 representations. Their `self` link returns the
paginated contents of the directory. The `meta` link on the other hand
returns the actual `directory` object itself, e.g.:

```javascript
{
  "path": "tests/test_project",
  "type": "commit_directory",
  "links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/test_project/"
    },
    "meta": {
      "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/atlassian/bbql/src/eefd5ef5d3df01aed629f650959d6706d54cd335/tests/test_project/?format=meta"
    }
  },
  "commit": { ... }
}
```

#### Querying, filtering and sorting

Like most API endpoints, this API supports the Bitbucket
querying/filtering syntax and so you could filter a directory listing
to only include entries that match certain criteria. For instance, to
list all binary files over 1kb use the expression:

`size > 1024 and attributes = "binary"`

which after urlencoding yields the query string:

`?q=size%3E1024+and+attributes%3D%22binary%22`

To change the ordering of the response, use the `?sort` parameter:

`.../src/eefd5ef/?sort=-size`

See [filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) for more
details.

<h3 id="get-file-or-directory-contents-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|format|query|string|false|If 'meta' is provided, returns the (json) meta data for the contents of the file.  If 'rendered' is provided, returns the contents of a non-binary file in HTML-formatted rendered markup. Since Git does not generally track what text encoding scheme is used, this endpoint attempts to detect the most appropriate character encoding. While usually correct, determining the character encoding can be ambiguous which in exceptional cases can lead to misinterpretation of the characters. As such, the raw element in the response object should not be treated as equivalent to the file's actual contents.|
|q|query|string|false|Optional filter expression as per [filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering).|
|sort|query|string|false|Optional sorting parameter as per [filtering and sorting](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#sorting-query-results).|
|max_depth|query|integer|false|If provided, returns the contents of the repository and its subdirectories recursively until the specified max_depth of nested directories. When omitted, this defaults to 1.|
|commit|path|string|true|The commit's SHA1.|
|path|path|string|true|Path to the file.|
|repo_slug|path|string|true|This can either be the repository slug or the UUID of the repository,<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{repository UUID}`.<br>|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|meta|
|format|rendered|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "next": "http://example.com",
  "page": 1,
  "pagelen": 1,
  "previous": "http://example.com",
  "size": 0,
  "values": [
    {
      "commit": {
        "participants": [
          {
            "type": "string",
            "approved": true,
            "participated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "role": "PARTICIPANT",
            "state": "approved",
            "user": {
              "type": "string",
              "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
              "display_name": "string",
              "links": {
                "avatar": {
                  "href": "http://example.com",
                  "name": "string"
                }
              },
              "username": "string",
              "uuid": "string"
            }
          }
        ],
        "repository": {}
      },
      "path": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

> 555 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-file-or-directory-contents-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|If the path matches a file, then the raw contents of the file are<br>returned.  If the `format=meta` query parameter is provided,<br>a json document containing the file's meta data is<br>returned.  If the `format=rendered` query parameter is provided,<br>the contents of the file in HTML-formated rendered markup is returned.<br>If the path matches a directory, then a paginated<br>list of file and directory entries is returned (if the<br>`format=meta` query parameter was provided, then the json document<br>containing the directory's meta data is returned.)<br>|[paginated_treeentries](#schemapaginated_treeentries)|
|404|Not Found|If the path or commit in the URL does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|555|555|If the call times out, possibly because the specified recursion depth is too large.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2 ( Scopes: repository ), basic, api_key
</aside>

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-ssh">Ssh</h1>

The SSH resource allows you to manage SSH keys.


## List SSH keys

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/string/ssh-keys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/{selected_user}/ssh-keys`

Returns a paginated list of the user's SSH public keys.

Example:

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/users/{ed08f5e1-605b-4f4a-aee4-6c97628a673e}/ssh-keys

    "pagelen": 10,
    "size": 1,

            "comment": "user@myhost",
            "created_on": "2018-03-14T13:17:05.196003+00:00",
            "key": "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIKqP3Cr632C2dNhhgKVcon4ldUSAeKiku2yP9O9/bDtY",
            "label": "",
            "last_used": "2018-03-20T13:18:05.196003+00:00",
            "links": {
                "self": {
                    "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/users/{ed08f5e1-605b-4f4a-aee4-6c97628a673e}/ssh-keys/b15b6026-9c02-4626-b4ad-b905f99f763a"
                }
            },
            "owner": {
                "display_name": "Mark Adams",
                "links": {
                    "avatar": {
                        "href": "https://bitbucket.org/account/markadams-atl/avatar/32/"
                    },
                    "html": {
                        "href": "https://bitbucket.org/markadams-atl/"
                    },
                    "self": {
                        "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/users/{ed08f5e1-605b-4f4a-aee4-6c97628a673e}"

}
```

## Add a new SSH key

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/string/ssh-keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "key": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "last_used": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "links": {
      "self": {
        "href": "http://example.com",
        "name": "string"
      }
    },
    "uuid": "string",
    "owner": {
      "type": "string",
      "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "display_name": "string",
      "links": {
        "avatar": {
          "href": "http://example.com",
          "name": "string"
        }
      },
      "username": "string",
      "uuid": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /users/{selected_user}/ssh-keys`

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-webhooks">Webhooks</h1>

Webhooks provide a way to configure Bitbucket Cloud to make requests to
your server (or another external service) whenever certain events occur in
Bitbucket Cloud.

A webhook consists of:

* A subject -- The resource that generates the events. Currently, this resource
is the repository, user account, or team where you create the webhook.
* One or more event -- The default event is a repository push, but you can
select multiple events that can trigger the webhook.
* A URL -- The endpoint where you want Bitbucket to send the event payloads
when a matching event happens.

There are two parts to getting a webhook to work: creating the webhook and
triggering the webhook. After you create a webhook for an event, every time
that event occurs, Bitbucket sends a payload request that describes the event
to the specified URL. Thus, you can think of webhooks as a kind of
notification system.

Use webhooks to integrate applications with Bitbucket Cloud. The following
use cases provides examples of when you would want to use webhooks:

* Every time a user pushes commits in a repository, you may want to notify
your CI server to start a build.
* Every time a user pushes commits or creates a pull request, you may want to
display a notification in your application.


## Get a webhook resource

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/hook_events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /hook_events`

Returns the webhook resource or subject types on which webhooks can
be registered.

Each resource/subject type contains an `events` link that returns the
paginated list of specific events each individual subject type can
emit.

This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require
authentication or scopes.

Example:

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/hook_events

{
    "repository": {
        "links": {
            "events": {
                "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/hook_events/repository"
            }
        }
    },
    "workspace": {
        "links": {
            "events": {
                "href": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/hook_events/workspace"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "repository": {
    "events": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    }
  },
  "workspace": {
    "events": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-webhook-resource-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## List subscribable webhook types

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/hook_events/repository \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /hook_events/{subject_type}`

Returns a paginated list of all valid webhook events for the
specified entity.
**The team and user webhooks are deprecated, and you should use workspace instead.
For more information, see [the announcement](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/bitbucket-api-teams-deprecation/).**

This is public data that does not require any scopes or authentication.

Example:

NOTE: The following example is a truncated response object for the `workspace` `subject_type`.
We return the same structure for the other `subject_type` objects.

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/hook_events/workspace
{
    "page": 1,
    "pagelen": 30,

    "values": [
        {

}
```

<h1 id="bitbucket-api-workspaces">Workspaces</h1>

A workspace is where you create repositories, collaborate on
your code, and organize different streams of work in your Bitbucket
Cloud account. Workspaces replace the use of teams and users in API
calls.


## List workspaces for the current user

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/permissions/workspaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /user/permissions/workspaces`

Returns an object for each workspace the caller is a member of, and
their effective role - the highest level of privilege the caller has.
If a user is a member of multiple groups with distinct roles, only the
highest level is returned.

Permissions can be:

* `owner`
* `collaborator`
* `member`

**The `collaborator` role is being removed from the Bitbucket Cloud API. For more information,
see the [deprecation announcement](/cloud/bitbucket/deprecation-notice-collaborator-role/).**

Example:

```
$ curl https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/user/permissions/workspaces

{
  "pagelen": 10,
  "page": 1,
  "size": 1,
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "workspace_membership",
      "permission": "owner",
      "last_accessed": "2019-03-07T12:35:02.900024+00:00",
      "added_on": "2018-10-11T17:42:02.961424+00:00",
      "user": {
        "type": "user",
        "uuid": "{470c176d-3574-44ea-bb41-89e8638bcca4}",
        "nickname": "evzijst",
        "display_name": "Erik van Zijst",
      },
      "workspace": {
        "type": "workspace",
        "uuid": "{a15fb181-db1f-48f7-b41f-e1eff06929d6}",
        "slug": "bbworkspace1",
        "name": "Atlassian Bitbucket",
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Results may be further [filtered or sorted](/cloud/bitbucket/rest/intro/#filtering) by
workspace or permission by adding the following query string parameters:

* `q=workspace.slug="bbworkspace1"` or `q=permission="owner"`
* `sort=workspace.slug`

Note that the query parameter values need to be URL escaped so that `=`
would become `%3D`.

<h3 id="list-workspaces-for-the-current-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Create a webhook for a workspace

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/workspaces/string/hooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /workspaces/{workspace}/hooks`

Creates a new webhook on the specified workspace.

Workspace webhooks are fired for events from all repositories contained
by that workspace.

Example:

```
$ curl -X POST -u credentials -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/workspaces/my-workspace/hooks
  -d '
    {
      "description": "Webhook Description",
      "url": "https://example.com/",
      "active": true,
      "events": [
        "repo:push",
        "issue:created",
        "issue:updated"
      ]
    }'
```

This call requires the webhook scope, as well as any scope
that applies to the events that the webhook subscribes to. In the
example above that means: `webhook`, `repository` and `issue`.

The `url` must properly resolve and cannot be an internal, non-routed address.

Only workspace owners can install webhooks on workspaces.

<h3 id="create-a-webhook-for-a-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace|path|string|true|This can either be the workspace ID (slug) or the workspace UUID<br>surrounded by curly-braces, for example: `{workspace UUID}`.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "active": true,
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "description": "string",
  "events": [
    "pullrequest:changes_request_created"
  ],
  "subject": {
    "type": "string"
  },
  "subject_type": "repository",
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "uuid": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "data": {},
    "detail": "string",
    "message": "string"
  },
  "type": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-webhook-for-a-workspace-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|If the webhook was registered successfully.|[webhook_subscription](#schemawebhook_subscription)|
|403|Forbidden|If the authenticated user does not have permission to install webhooks on the specified workspace.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|If the specified workspace does not exist.|[error](#schemaerror)|

## List all repository permissions for a workspace

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/workspaces/string/permissions/repositories \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /workspaces/{workspace}/permissions/repositories`

Returns an object for each repository permission for all of a
workspace's repositories.

Permissions returned are effective permissions: the highest level of
permission the user has. This does not distinguish between direct and
indirect (group) privileges.

Only users with admin permission for the team may access this resource.

Permissions can be:

* `admin`
* `write`
* `read`

Example:


<h1 id="bitbucket-api-search">Search</h1>

## Search for code in a team's repositories

<a id="opIdsearchTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/teams/string/search/code?search_query=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /teams/{username}/search/code`

Search for code in the repositories of the specified team.

Searching across all repositories:

```
curl 'https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/teams/team_name/search/code?search_query=foo'
{
  "size": 1,
  "page": 1,
  "pagelen": 10,
  "query_substituted": false,
  "values": [
    {
      "type": "code_search_result",
```

# Schemas

<h2 id="tocS_account">account</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaaccount"></a>
<a id="schema_account"></a>
<a id="tocSaccount"></a>
<a id="tocsaccount"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "display_name": "string",
  "links": {
    "avatar": {
      "href": "http://example.com",
      "name": "string"
    }
  },
  "username": "string",
  "uuid": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|created_on|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|display_name|string|false|none|none|
|links|[account_links](#schemaaccount_links)|false|none|Links related to an Account.|

```json
    "public"
  ]
}
```

An application property. It is a caller defined JSON object that Bitbucket will store and return. 
The `_attributes` field at its top level can be used to control who is allowed to read and update the property. 
The keys of the JSON object must match an allowed pattern. For details, 
see [Application properties](/cloud/bitbucket/application-properties/).

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|type|string|true|none|none|

|description|string|false|none|A description of the build (e.g. "Unit tests in Bamboo")|
|key|string|false|none|An identifier for the status that's unique to<br>        its type (current "build" is the only supported type) and the vendor,<br>        e.g. BB-DEPLOY|

This optional field can be useful for build systems whose<br>build triggers and configuration are branch-dependent (e.g. a Pipeline<br>build).<br>It is legitimate for this field to not be set, or even apply (e.g. a<br>static linting job).|
|state|string|false|none|Provides some indication of the status of this commit|
|updated_on|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|url|string|false|none|A URL linking back to the vendor or build system, for providing more information about whatever process produced this status. Accepts context variables `repository` and `commit` that Bitbucket will evaluate at runtime whenever at runtime. For example, one could use https://foo.com/builds/{repository.full_name} which Bitbucket will turn into https://foo.com/builds/foo/bar at render time.|

|owner|[team](#schemateam)|false|none|none|
|updated_on|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|uuid|string|false|none|The project's immutable id.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|author|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|none|
|close_source_branch|boolean|false|none|A boolean flag indicating if merging the pull request closes the source branch.|
|closed_by|[account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|none|
|comment_count|integer|false|none|The number of comments for a specific pull request.|
|created_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was created.|
|destination|[pullrequest_endpoint](#schemapullrequest_endpoint)|false|none|none|
|id|integer|false|none|The pull request's unique ID. Note that pull request IDs are only unique within their associated repository.|
|links|object|false|none|none|
|merge_commit|object|false|none|none|
|participants|[[participant](#schemaparticipant)]|false|none|        The list of users that are collaborating on this pull request.<br>        Collaborators are user that:<br><br>        * are added to the pull request as a reviewer (part of the reviewers<br>          list)<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have commented on the pull request<br>        * are not explicit reviewers, but have approved the pull request<br><br>        Each user is wrapped in an object that indicates the user's role and<br>        whether they have approved the pull request. For performance reasons,<br>        the API only returns this list when an API requests a pull request by<br>        id.<br>        |
|reason|string|false|none|Explains why a pull request was declined. This field is only applicable to pull requests in rejected state.|
|rendered|object|false|none|User provided pull request text, interpreted in a markup language and rendered in HTML|
|reviewers|[[account](#schemaaccount)]|false|none|The list of users that were added as reviewers on this pull request when it was created. For performance reasons, the API only includes this list on a pull request's `self` URL.|
|source|[pullrequest_endpoint](#schemapullrequest_endpoint)|false|none|none|
|state|string|false|none|The pull request's current status.|
|summary|object|false|none|none|
|task_count|integer|false|none|The number of open tasks for a specific pull request.|
|title|string|false|none|Title of the pull request.|
|updated_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The ISO8601 timestamp the request was last updated.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|OPEN|
|state|MERGED|
|state|DECLINED|
|state|SUPERSEDED|

<h2 id="tocS_pullrequest_merge_parameters">pullrequest_merge_parameters</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapullrequest_merge_parameters"></a>
<a id="schema_pullrequest_merge_parameters"></a>
<a id="tocSpullrequest_merge_parameters"></a>
<a id="tocspullrequest_merge_parameters"></a>

```json
{
  "close_source_branch": true,
  "merge_strategy": "merge_commit",
  "message": "string",
  "type": "string"
}
```

The metadata that describes a pull request merge.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|close_source_branch|boolean|false|none|Whether the source branch should be deleted. If this is not provided, we fallback to the value used when the pull request was created, which defaults to False|
|merge_strategy|string|false|none|The merge strategy that will be used to merge the pull request.|
|message|string|false|none|The commit message that will be used on the resulting commit.|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|merge_strategy|merge_commit|
|merge_strategy|squash|
|merge_strategy|fast_forward|

```json
      "value": {}
    }
  ],
  "details": "string",
  "external_id": "string",
  "link": "http://example.com",
  "logo_url": "http://example.com",
  "remote_link_enabled": true,
  "report_type": "SECURITY",

  "result": "PASSED",
  "title": "string",
  "updated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "uuid": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|created_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp when the report was created.|
|data|[[report_data](#schemareport_data)]|false|none|An array of data fields to display information on the report. Maximum 10.|
|details|string|false|none|A string to describe the purpose of the report.|
|external_id|string|false|none|ID of the report provided by the report creator. It can be used to identify the report as an alternative to it's generated uuid. It is not used by Bitbucket, but only by the report creator for updating or deleting this specific report. Needs to be unique.|
|link|string(uri)|false|none|A URL linking to the results of the report in an external tool.|
|logo_url|string(uri)|false|none|A URL to the report logo. If none is provided, the default insights logo will be used.|
|remote_link_enabled|boolean|false|none|If enabled, a remote link is created in Jira for the issue associated with the commit the report belongs to.|
|report_type|string|false|none|The type of the report.|
|reporter|string|false|none|A string to describe the tool or company who created the report.|
|result|string|false|none|The state of the report. May be set to PENDING and later updated.|
|title|string|false|none|The title of the report.|
|updated_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp when the report was updated.|
|uuid|string|false|none|The UUID that can be used to identify the report.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|report_type|SECURITY|
|report_type|COVERAGE|
|report_type|TEST|
|report_type|BUG|
|result|PASSED|
|result|FAILED|
|result|PENDING|

<h2 id="tocS_report_annotation">report_annotation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareport_annotation"></a>
<a id="schema_report_annotation"></a>
<a id="tocSreport_annotation"></a>
<a id="tocsreport_annotation"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "string",
  "annotation_type": "VULNERABILITY",
  "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "details": "string",
  "external_id": "string",
  "line": 1,
  "link": "http://example.com",
  "path": "string",
  "result": "PASSED",
  "severity": "CRITICAL",
  "summary": "string",
  "updated_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "uuid": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|annotation_type|string|false|none|The type of the report.|
|created_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp when the report was created.|
|details|string|false|none|The details to show to users when clicking on the annotation.|
|external_id|string|false|none|ID of the annotation provided by the annotation creator. It can be used to identify the annotation as an alternative to it's generated uuid. It is not used by Bitbucket, but only by the annotation creator for updating or deleting this specific annotation. Needs to be unique.|
|line|integer|false|none|The line number that the annotation should belong to. If no line number is provided, then it will default to 0 and in a pull request it will appear at the top of the file specified by the path field.|
|link|string(uri)|false|none|A URL linking to the annotation in an external tool.|
|path|string|false|none|The path of the file on which this annotation should be placed. This is the path of the file relative to the git repository. If no path is provided, then it will appear in the overview modal on all pull requests where the tip of the branch is the given commit, regardless of which files were modified.|
|result|string|false|none|The state of the report. May be set to PENDING and later updated.|
|severity|string|false|none|The severity of the annotation.|
|summary|string|false|none|The message to display to users.|
|updated_on|string(date-time)|false|none|The timestamp when the report was updated.|
|uuid|string|false|none|The UUID that can be used to identify the annotation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|annotation_type|VULNERABILITY|
|annotation_type|CODE_SMELL|
|annotation_type|BUG|
|result|PASSED|
|result|FAILED|
|result|SKIPPED|
|result|IGNORED|
|severity|CRITICAL|
|severity|HIGH|
|severity|MEDIUM|
|severity|LOW|
